symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Known Hölder smoothness exponent \(\alpha\) of the propensity calibration.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Known Hölder smoothness exponent \(\beta\) of each outcome regression.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: Arbitrary probability law \(Q\) on the complete record space.

symbols.name: H_s_L
symbols.def: For a positive exponent \(s\), \(\mathcal H^s(L)\) contains functions whose partial derivatives through order \(m=\lceil s\rceil-1\) are bounded by \(L\) and whose order-\(m\) derivatives have \(s-m\) Hölder seminorm at most \(L\) under the sup norm.

symbols.name: mu_a
symbols.def: Clean outcome-regression functions \(\mu_a\) on \(\mathcal X\); wherever \(P(A=a\mid X=x)>0\), \(\mu_a(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x,A=a]\).

symbols.name: theta_F
symbols.def: Full-data average treatment effect \(\theta^{\mathrm F}(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(1)-Y(0)]\).

symbols.name: P_prime
symbols.def: A second clean observed law \(P'\) used in pairwise comparisons.

symbols.name: delta_0
symbols.def: Positive local radius \(\delta_0\) depending only on the fixed class parameters.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Localization scale \(h\) for the one-dimensional least-favorable pair.

symbols.name: R_n
symbols.def: Minimax absolute risk \(\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon)\) defined by \(\texttt{def:minimax-risk}\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Generic measurable subset \(B\) of the record space.

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Auxiliary binary response \(Z\) drawn conditionally as \(Z\mid O\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(Y)\).

symbols.name: mathsf_Ber
symbols.def: Markov kernel replacing \(Y=y\) by an independent \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(y)\) while retaining \(X,A\).

symbols.name: mathcal_D_n
symbols.def: When \(h_n=2^{-J}\), set \(r_j=2^jh_n\) and \(M_j=\lceil\sqrt{r_j}/h_n\rceil\) for \(j=0,\ldots,J-1\). For \(k=0,\ldots,M_j-1\), let \(D_{j,k}=[r_j+kr_j/M_j,r_j+(k+1)r_j/M_j)\), except that \(D_{J-1,M_{J-1}-1}\) includes its right endpoint \(1\). The disjoint collection \(\mathcal D_n=\{D_{j,k}:0\leq j<J,0\leq k<M_j\}\) partitions \([h_n,1]\).

symbols.name: mhat_a
symbols.def: For every Borel cell \(D\subseteq[0,1]\), let \(N_a(D)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in D,A_i=a\}\). Set \(\widehat m_a(D)=N_a(D)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in D,A_i=a\}\) when \(N_a(D)>0\), and set \(\widehat m_a(D)=1/2\) when \(N_a(D)=0\); hence \(\widehat m_a(D)\in[0,1]\).

symbols.name: T_Lip
symbols.def: Clipped variable-width cell estimator \(T_{\mathrm{Lip}}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1/2,1/2]}[\sum_{D\in\mathcal D_n}|D|\{\widehat m_1(D)-\widehat m_0(D)\}+h_n\{\widehat m_1(B_n)-\widehat m_0(B_n)\}]\), returning \(0\) when \(b_n>1/4\).

symbols.name: mathfrak_H_rob
symbols.def: Dyadic weak-overlap slab decomposition with Hölder boundary moment reproduction, sample splitting, bounded-discrepancy robust estimation of nuisance and Gram moments, and an off-diagonal projected correction analyzed by a contaminated Hoeffding decomposition.

symbols.name: rho_eval
symbols.def: DERIVED by \(\texttt{oeq:full-frontier}\): the explicit deterministic piecewise rate \(\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}(n,\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\), including logarithmic factors at equality boundaries.

symbols.name: T_star
symbols.def: DERIVED by \(\texttt{oeq:full-frontier}\) from the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rob}}\): a total finite Borel estimator \(T^\star_n\) with explicit tuning, zero-count fallbacks, arithmetic complexity, and memory complexity.

assumptions.condition: Under \(P\), the covariate \(X\) is exactly uniform on \(\mathcal X=[0,1]^d\).
The clean propensity satisfies \(e(x)=x_1^\kappa u(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

novel.justification: This controlled boundary-selection benchmark represents treatment access that turns on polynomially with a scalar distance-to-access coordinate while allowing smooth heterogeneity through \(u\).

assumptions.condition: The calibration obeys \(1/4\leq u(x)\leq1/2\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

novel.justification: This scale normalization keeps interior treatment intensity nondegenerate and contains constant calibrations \(u=1/4\) and \(u=1/2\) together with smooth bounded perturbations.

assumptions.condition: For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(P(A=a\mid X=x)>0\), \(\mu_a(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x,A=a]\).

standard.name: Conditional-mean version on the positive-probability region

assumptions.condition: For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the regression satisfies \(\mu_a\in\mathcal H^\beta(L)\).
For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the regression obeys \(1/4\leq\mu_a(x)\leq3/4\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The observed outcome satisfies \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\) under \(P^{\mathrm F}\).
The potential-outcome pair satisfies \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\) under \(P^{\mathrm F}\).
The records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent with common law \(R\).

definitions.name: mathcal_C_eps
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L}(\epsilon)=\{(P,Q,R):P\in\mathcal P_{d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L},\ Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal O),\ R=(1-\epsilon)P+\epsilon Q\}\).

definitions.name: mathsf_Ber
definitions.construction: Given \(O=(X,A,Y)\), draw \(Z\mid O\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(Y)\) independently and output \((X,A,Z)\); derandomize any bounded binary-response estimator by its finite conditional expectation over \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\).

definitions.name: T_Lip
definitions.construction: Set \(b_n=\max\{n^{-1/5},\epsilon^{1/4}\}\) and return \(0\) if \(b_n>1/4\). Otherwise let \(h_n\) be the least dyadic number at least \(b_n\), construct the explicitly endpointed cells \(\mathcal D_n\), compute every bounded zero-safe arm mean \(\widehat m_a(D)\), reuse \(B_n=[h_n,2h_n]\) for boundary reconstruction, and return \(T_{\mathrm{Lip}}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1/2,1/2]}[\sum_{D\in\mathcal D_n}|D|\{\widehat m_1(D)-\widehat m_0(D)\}+h_n\{\widehat m_1(B_n)-\widehat m_0(B_n)\}]\). A single pass assigns records to slabs and cells and accumulates arm counts and outcome sums.

definitions.name: P_h_pair
definitions.construction: For \(0<h\leq1/4\), define clean binary-outcome laws \(P_{0,h}\) and \(P_{1,h}\) by \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1])\), \(u(x)=1/2\), \(e(x)=x^2/2\), \(Y\mid(X=x,A=0)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(Y\mid(X=x,A=1)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_{1,j}(x))\), \(\mu_{1,0}(x)=1/2\), and \(\mu_{1,1}(x)=1/2+(h-x)_+/4\). Let \(t=\operatorname{TV}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\), and let \(S_+\) and \(S_-\) be the probability normalizations of the positive and negative parts of \(P_{1,h}-P_{0,h}\). Whenever \(\epsilon>0\) and \(t\leq\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\), set \(c=(1-\epsilon)t/\epsilon\), \(H=P_{0,h}\), \(Q_{0,h}=cS_++(1-c)H\), \(Q_{1,h}=cS_-+(1-c)H\), and \(R_h=(1-\epsilon)P_{0,h}+\epsilon Q_{0,h}=(1-\epsilon)P_{1,h}+\epsilon Q_{1,h}\).

definitions.name: mathfrak_H_rob
definitions.construction: Start from the exact slabwise projected nuisance-product identity; reproduce the missing boundary moments by a finite polynomial system; estimate pilot vectors and Gram moments by bounded-discrepancy minimum-distance projection on sample splits; form bounded off-diagonal corrected pairs; test both point and diffuse within-cell contamination; and bound clean, contaminating, and mixed Hoeffding components under one global \(Q\)-mass budget before optimizing slab and projection resolutions.

statements.statement: Under the known uniform design, consistency, and conditional exchangeability, the causal ATE equals the clean observed-law functional: \(\theta^{\mathrm F}(P^{\mathrm F})=\theta(P)=\int_{[0,1]^d}\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}\,\mathrm dx\).
statements.justification: This standard supporting result separates causal identification under the clean law from the contaminated-sampling decision problem.
statements.gap: RosenbaumRubin1983 supplies the standard identification bridge, and the known uniform design converts the covariate expectation to the displayed Lebesgue integral; no novelty is claimed for this proposition.
statements.consumer: The proposition lets applied ATE users interpret the statistical radius without asserting point identification of the clean law from \(R\).

statements.statement: For every \(n\geq2\) and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/10\), applying \(\mathsf{Ber}\) to the bounded-outcome Huber experiment preserves \(\theta(P)\), maps every admissible \(Q\) to an admissible binary-response contaminant, and leaves the minimax absolute risk \(\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\) unchanged after finite derandomization.
statements.justification: The reduction removes unrestricted conditional outcome distributions without changing the decision problem.
statements.gap: ChenGaoRen2016 treats generic clean laws but does not give this causal bounded-to-binary exact experiment reduction.
statements.consumer: A finite categorical representation makes same-experiment lower witnesses and computable sieves possible.

statements.statement: There exist \(c_0,C_0>0\) and \(\delta_0>0\), depending only on \(d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L\), such that for every \(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\), \[c_0\delta^{\gamma_{\mathrm{TV}}}\leq\omega_\theta(\delta)\leq C_0\delta^{\gamma_{\mathrm{TV}}},\qquad \gamma_{\mathrm{TV}}=\frac{\beta+1}{\beta+\kappa+1}.\] The exponent is uniform in the propensity calibration \(u\), is unchanged when \(P\) and \(P'\) have different propensities, and does not depend on \(\alpha\) or \(d\).
statements.justification: This theorem derives the irreducible population ambiguity caused jointly by weak overlap and full-record contamination.
statements.gap: ChenGaoRen2016 identifies the total-variation modulus as the robust lower-bound object, but neither evaluates it for this ATE class nor handles simultaneous propensity changes.
statements.consumer: The modulus gives the mandatory corruption-radius floor for any error bar supplied alongside SasakiUra2022Robustate.

statements.statement: For every \(0<h\leq1/4\), both members of \(P_h^{\mathrm{pair}}=(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{1,1,1,2,L}\), and \[|\theta(P_{1,h})-\theta(P_{0,h})|=h^2/8,\qquad \operatorname{TV}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})=h^4/96,\qquad \operatorname{KL}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\leq h^5/240.\] For \(n\geq4^5\), \(h=n^{-1/5}\) gives the clean two-point lower rate \(n^{-2/5}\), while \(h=1/4\) covers the remaining finite set of sample sizes after adjusting the constant. With \(h=\{\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\}^{1/4}/4\), the explicit contaminants satisfy \(R_h=(1-\epsilon)P_{0,h}+\epsilon Q_{0,h}=(1-\epsilon)P_{1,h}+\epsilon Q_{1,h}\), and the clean targets are separated by a constant multiple of \(\{\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\}^{1/2}\).
statements.justification: The explicit pair certifies both the clean and contamination components inside the same declared experiment rather than importing an unmatched oracle lower bound.
statements.gap: ChenGaoRen2016 gives the abstract Huber-neighborhood intersection device, but not a pair satisfying the exact uniform-design, polynomial-overlap, Hölder, and bounded-regression restrictions.
statements.consumer: The pair supplies the same-experiment converse for the one-dimensional calibration theorem and a required lower-bound test for the general frontier.

statements.statement: On the full declared class with \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1\), and \(\kappa=2\), there exist \(c_0,C_0>0\), depending only on \(L\), such that jointly for every \(n\geq2\) and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/10\), \[c_0\{n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\}\leq\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;1,1,1,2,L)\leq\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{1,1,1,2,L}(\epsilon)}\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_{\mathrm{Lip}}-\theta(P)|\leq C_0\{n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\}.\] When \(b_n\leq1/4\), the sharper pre-optimization bound is \[\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{1,1,1,2,L}(\epsilon)}\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_{\mathrm{Lip}}-\theta(P)|\leq C_0\left[h_n^2+(nh_n)^{-1/2}+\epsilon h_n^{-2}+\exp\{-c_0nh_n^{7/2}\}\right].\] For each body cell \(D\subseteq[r_j,2r_j]\), writing \(q_D=Q\{X\in D\}\), its weighted contamination shift is at most \(C_0\epsilon q_D/r_j^2\), and \(\sum_Dq_D\leq1\); the reused boundary slab \(B_n\) contributes at most \(C_0\epsilon q_{B_n}/h_n^2\). These bounds depend only on total contaminating mass and therefore cover both point masses and diffuse within-cell contamination. The estimator uses \(O(n\log(1/h_n)+h_n^{-1})\) arithmetic operations and \(O(h_n^{-1})\) memory.
statements.justification: This field-tier calibration theorem shows on an exact weak-overlap class that one finite estimator simultaneously attains the clean \(n^{-2/5}\) difficulty and the \(\epsilon^{1/2}\) contamination ambiguity.
statements.gap: Section 3 and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 of MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 establish trimmed bias-corrected doubly robust asymptotics for clean i.i.d. records; they do not permit arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\) or provide this same-class contaminated minimax equality.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives SasakiUra2022Robustate a quantitative boundary-correction and error-radius benchmark for separating limited overlap from unreliable records.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rob}}\), determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}(n,\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\) and construct \(T_n^\star\) so that, jointly for all \(n\geq2\) and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/10\), \[c_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}\leq\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\leq\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L}(\epsilon)}\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_n^\star-\theta(P)|\leq C_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}.\] The rate must be an explicit finite piecewise formula with every equality-case logarithm; the estimator must be total, finite, data-only, and computationally specified; and the converse must use the same contaminated experiment. The result must decide whether the clean functional rate and \(\omega_\theta(\epsilon/(1-\epsilon))\) are simultaneously attainable or whether a quantified nuisance-contamination interaction term is unavoidable.
statements.justification: This first-class open extension asks whether the simultaneous attainment proved by the one-dimensional calibration persists across the full multidimensional smoothness phase diagram.
statements.gap: Section 3 of MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 starts from clean i.i.d. observations and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies its ATE trimming and boundary-bias conditions; neither allows arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). ChenGaoRen2016 gives generic Huber testing, and RobinsEtAl2017HOEE gives clean higher-order correction, but neither supplies the requested robust fast-functional construction and same-experiment Huber-neighborhood converse on this boundary class.
statements.consumer: SasakiUra2022Robustate gains a theoretical error-radius and boundary-correction benchmark that separates limited-overlap robustness from unreliable-record robustness.

sampling_model.design: Known clean design \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), observed only through a full-record Huber mixture.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) observed records are independent draws from \(R=(1-\epsilon)P+\epsilon Q\).
sampling_model.overlap: The propensity vanishes only on the boundary \(x_1=0\) and has polynomial order \(\kappa\) with calibration in \([1/4,1/2]\).
sampling_model.outcome: The clean outcome is bounded in \([0,1]\); only its two conditional means are Hölder-restricted.
sampling_model.contamination: The law \(Q\) may jointly corrupt \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\), including by placing atoms on the clean null boundary.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \(d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L,\epsilon\) and the clean covariate design, but not \(P,Q,u,\mu_0,\mu_1\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Unbounded inverse weights can make a point-identified treatment-effect parameter irregular, with rates governed by relative tail behavior.
Huber minimax lower bounds are governed by the clean risk and a total-variation modulus, while Scheffé tournaments attain optimal full-law total-variation rates.
Projection-based higher-order influence-function estimators attain optimal clean rates for missing-response means under low nuisance regularity.
An empirically estimated Gram operator yields a semiparametrically efficient clean higher-order estimator without smoothness of the covariate density.
Density-power IPW and doubly robust equations resist outcome outliers under stronger overlap and require an additional correction to retain double robustness.
A second-order correction can match an ATE nuisance-product frontier in a clean hybrid smoothness and structure-agnostic model.
Bias-corrected trimming supports ATE estimation and inference under limited overlap and is implemented for right-heart-catheterization data.
Low-rank structure permits data cleaning and causal inference under structured measurement error, missingness, discretization, and privacy noise with bounded propensities.
Section 3 constructs a trimmed bias-corrected doubly robust estimator from i.i.d. observations, and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies the ATE-specific boundary conditions under clean sampling.

tldr: On the exact one-dimensional Lipschitz boundary class with \(e(x)=x^2u(x)\), a total finite dyadic cell estimator attains the same-experiment minimax risk \(n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\) when an arbitrary Huber contaminant may replace \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). The theorem includes an explicit pre-optimization bound, global contaminant-mass accounting for point and diffuse corruption, and clean and neighborhood-colliding lower pairs. The causal bridge and total-variation modulus support this field-tier calibration, while the multidimensional smoothness phase diagram remains a first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Section 3 and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 of MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 analyze trimming and boundary bias correction under clean i.i.d. sampling, while robust causal estimators treat narrower outcome corruption under stronger overlap and generic Huber theory does not preserve fast scalar-functional structure. No located theorem gives a computable same-class minimax equality when the propensity vanishes quadratically and \(Q\) may replace \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\).
project_justification.niche: The missing field-tier benchmark is a boundary reconstruction that remains stable when contaminating mass is concentrated exactly in its lowest-occupancy slab, with a converse built inside the same full-record mixture experiment.
project_justification.fill: The dyadic estimator uses variable-width cells, bounded zero-count-safe arm means, and a reused first slab to attain \(n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\). Exact clean-law pairs certify the clean and contamination lower bounds, and the remaining multidimensional projection frontier is stated separately as open content.

related_work: MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 is the nearest clean-record comparator. Section 3 defines its trimming and bias-corrected estimator from i.i.d. observations, and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies the ATE-specific boundary conditions; neither part allows arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). KhanTamer2010 establishes generic support-tail irregularity for inverse weighting but does not supply the controlled factorization \(e(x)=x_1^\kappa u(x)\), its calibration envelope, or a contaminated minimax theorem. ChenGaoRen2016 supplies robust tests and the Huber-neighborhood total-variation-modulus template, while its constructive upper theorem estimates whole laws rather than this scalar ATE at its clean functional rate. RobinsEtAl2017HOEE and LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF supply projection and empirical Gram constructions under clean sampling; they inform only the open multidimensional route. BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024 clarifies clean second-order ATE correction under interior overlap. HaradaFujisawa2024 controls outcome outliers but excludes arbitrary covariate and treatment-label replacement. MaEtAl2024Missing studies finite-coordinate missingness rather than continuous selection at a propensity zero. AgarwalSingh2022 uses structured low-rank corruption and bounded propensity. SasakiUra2022ET and SasakiUra2022Robustate motivate trimming and boundary correction under clean records, with the latter supplying the right-heart-catheterization consumer. HorowitzManski1995 explains why fixed contamination leaves irreducible ambiguity in the clean target.
technical_internal_limitation: Boundary-contamination diagnostic: for \(B=[h,2h]\), \(u=1/4\), clean treated-arm mean \(1/2\), and \(Q=\delta_{(h,1,1)}\), the clean treated mass in \(B\) is \(7h^3/12\). The resulting population shift of the boundary contribution is exactly \(h\epsilon/[2\{(1-\epsilon)7h^3/12+\epsilon\}]\), which is of order \(h^2=\epsilon^{1/2}\) at \(h=\epsilon^{1/4}\); the same global \(Q\)-mass accounting in the theorem covers diffuse contamination within a cell.
honest_scope: The field-tier headline is exactly the one-dimensional calibration \(\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;1,1,1,2,L)\asymp_L n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\), with a total finite estimator and matching same-experiment converse authored as results to prove. The causal bridge is standard support, and the Bernoulli reduction and total-variation modulus are supporting results. The general \(d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa\) rate formula, equality-boundary logarithms, robust projected correction, and matching full-class converse remain open. For \(\epsilon=0\), the calibration reduces to the clean \(n^{-2/5}\) frontier; for fixed nonzero \(\epsilon\), no statement claims point identification of \(\theta(P)\) from \(R\).

s1-full-frontier.anchor: ChenGaoRen2016, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1--3.2, with KhanTamer2010 as the weak-overlap boundary anchor
s1-full-frontier.anchor_read: Opened the arXiv source for ChenGaoRen2016 and read the Introduction, the Scheffé test construction in equations (5)--(7), Theorems 2.1 and 3.1--3.2, their proofs section, and the closing application proof; opened KhanTamer2010's publisher record and accessible manuscript receipt for its inverse-weight rate construction and concluding rate-adaptive recommendation.
s1-full-frontier.question: Derive the exact minimax absolute-error frontier on the declared class, with a total finite estimator and matching same-experiment lower bounds, and decide whether a nuisance-contamination interaction occurs.
s1-full-frontier.first_changed_proof_step: ChenGaoRen2016 first covers the clean law in total variation; that step is too costly for a scalar ATE whose clean functional rate can be faster, so it must be replaced by direct robust projected-functional estimation before the modulus argument is attached.
s1-full-frontier.destination_search: Exact-title and target-method searches for weak overlap plus Huber contamination plus higher-order ATE correction found no matching paper; AgarwalSingh2022 was inspected and uses structured covariate error, low rank, and bounded propensity instead.
s1-full-frontier.cynical_objection: Immediate from ChenGaoRen2016 because robust risk is always the maximum of clean risk and a total-variation modulus.
s1-full-frontier.rebuttal: Their constructive upper bound controls full-law total variation; it does not yield a data-only scalar-functional estimator at the faster clean ATE rate, and the unknown weak-overlap nuisance correction may introduce an additional channel.

s2-robust-projection.anchor_read: Opened the empirical-HOIF arXiv source lineage, read its Introduction, the second-order projection kernel and bias identity, Theorems 3, 5, and 7, the Gram-estimation discussion, the Hoeffding variance proof, and the conclusion on data-driven basis selection.
s2-robust-projection.question: Construct a finite robust nuisance and Gram projection whose corrected pair term preserves the clean high-resolution gain under point and diffuse within-cell contamination.
s2-robust-projection.first_changed_proof_step: The first clean step controlling the empirical Gram inverse fails because contaminated covariates can create leverage and contaminated pairs destroy conditional degeneracy.
s2-robust-projection.destination_search: The target-method search covered ZhuJiaoSteinhardt2022 generalized resilience, HaradaFujisawa2024 robust scores, BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024 clean second-order ATE correction, and the 2024 robust-functional conference title; no public theorem treats contaminated projection U-statistics at vanishing propensities.
s2-robust-projection.cynical_objection: Immediate by replacing every HOIF moment with a median-of-means estimate.
s2-robust-projection.rebuttal: Point and diffuse within-cell contamination can enter both arguments of a projected pair correction, destroy conditional degeneracy, and destabilize the empirical Gram operator; scalar median replacement does not by itself restore the clean cancellation.

s3-same-experiment-converse.anchor_read: Opened the cited prior-proposal proto cores and reviewer records identified in the gaps substrate, then opened the cited lower-bound exemplars RobinsEtAl2017HOEE and the localized fuzzy-hypothesis construction in KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024.
s3-same-experiment-converse.question: Build full-support Hölder alternatives and contaminants whose observed product experiments collide while their ATE separation realizes every clean, overlap, contamination, and interaction channel.
s3-same-experiment-converse.first_changed_proof_step: One-observation mixture cancellation must be replaced by an explicit bound for the shared-prior \(n\)-fold experiment while preserving exact-uniform \(X\) and the polynomial propensity factorization.
s3-same-experiment-converse.destination_search: Adjacent lower-bound scans covered the two-convex-mixture method, localized CATE fuzzy priors, structure-agnostic ATE lower bounds, and generic Huber neighborhood intersection; none enforces all declared clean-law constraints in the same contaminated experiment.
s3-same-experiment-converse.cynical_objection: Immediate by combining a clean minimax lower bound with the generic Huber modulus lower bound.
s3-same-experiment-converse.rebuttal: That maximum lower bound cannot certify a proposed interaction term and does not repair prior clean witnesses that violate the fixed uniform design or require unavailable reservoir richness.

s4-finite-cell.anchor_read: Opened the accepted prior-proposal proof summary and its finite heavy-light polynomial construction, then opened ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 for the sparse-cell lower-prior construction and discussion.
s4-finite-cell.question: Solve the exact finite boundary-slab problem with simultaneous cell rarity, treatment rarity, and arbitrary full-record contamination.
s4-finite-cell.first_changed_proof_step: The clean light-cell factorial-moment variance lemma must become a contamination-stable moment lemma uniform in the smallest treated-cell mass.
s4-finite-cell.destination_search: Searches for contaminated multinomial ATE polynomial estimators and robust factorial-moment lifting found robust distribution estimators but no joint causal cell-and-overlap theorem.
s4-finite-cell.cynical_objection: Immediate from the accepted clean heavy-light polynomial estimator plus clipping.
s4-finite-cell.rebuttal: Arbitrary \(Q\) can manufacture pilot counts and corrupt every factorial moment, invalidating both the heavy-light classification and unbiased lifts.

s5-sharp-interval.anchor_read: Opened the publisher and RePEc records, read the paper's identification argument and conclusion that bounds are the natural objects under contaminated sampling, and compared its domination construction with ChenGaoRen2016's Huber-neighborhood intersection theorem.
s5-sharp-interval.question: Characterize sharp contamination-compatible ATE endpoints under the exact Hölder and polynomial-overlap constraints and estimate them uniformly.
s5-sharp-interval.first_changed_proof_step: HorowitzManski1995 allocates contaminated mass without smoothness; the first changed step is the endpoint mass allocation, which becomes a coupled smooth-law domination problem.
s5-sharp-interval.destination_search: Searches included clean non-overlap bounds and contamination partial identification; no explicit smooth weak-overlap ATE endpoint formula was located.
s5-sharp-interval.cynical_objection: Immediate from the generic contaminated-sampling bounds by substituting the ATE range.
s5-sharp-interval.rebuttal: Exact-uniform design and coupled Hölder restrictions can sharply contract the generic missing-mass interval, so the endpoints require a new constrained extremal construction.

s6-local-efficiency.anchor_read: Opened the published abstract and accessible manuscript receipt for the zero-information and tail-rate argument, then read LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF's efficiency theorem and discussion.
s6-local-efficiency.question: For \(\epsilon_n=\gamma/\sqrt n\) in regular overlap-tail regimes, derive the local asymptotic minimax bias-variance envelope and an attaining robust ATE estimator.
s6-local-efficiency.first_changed_proof_step: The clean tangent-space efficiency calculation must be replaced by a shrinking gross-error tangent set whose support is amplified by \(x_1^{-\kappa}\).
s6-local-efficiency.destination_search: Searches for semiparametric efficiency under Huber neighborhoods and weak overlap found classical robust location efficiency and clean ATE efficiency, but no theorem for this boundary class.
s6-local-efficiency.cynical_objection: Immediate from Huber's clipped influence-function calculus applied to Hahn's ATE influence function.
s6-local-efficiency.rebuttal: The ATE influence function can have infinite variance and the clipping bias is constrained by Hölder boundary extrapolation, so the least-favorable tangent problem is not the regular interior-overlap calculation.

s7-limit-law.anchor_read: Opened the full publisher page and read the Introduction, equations (2)--(7), the bias-correction construction, the reported Theorem 4 asymptotic normality, the implementation section, the right-heart-catheterization discussion, and the conclusion.
s7-limit-law.question: Under shrinking \(\epsilon_n\) and polynomial overlap, derive the Gaussian or non-Gaussian limit of a contamination-stable boundary-corrected ATE estimator and uniform coverage transitions.
s7-limit-law.first_changed_proof_step: The clean trimmed-score linearization must first control adversarial bias at the same normalization before any triangular-array central limit theorem can be applied.
s7-limit-law.destination_search: Searches located clean trimmed-IPW limit laws and structured-corruption Gaussian approximations, but no arbitrary full-record Huber limit law at a propensity boundary.
s7-limit-law.cynical_objection: Immediate from SasakiUra2022ET after adding a bounded influence score.
s7-limit-law.rebuttal: A bounded score does not restore the clean target when contaminants change covariates and treatment labels, and the adversarial drift can be of the same order as the nonstandard normalization.

s8-policy-regret.anchor_read: Opened the arXiv source and read the Introduction, density-power IPW and doubly robust constructions, Theorems 1--6 and their estimating-equation proofs, the influence analysis, and the empirical conclusion.
s8-policy-regret.question: Choose a treatment policy from a Hölder decision class and derive its minimax welfare-regret frontier under weak overlap and arbitrary record corruption.
s8-policy-regret.first_changed_proof_step: The robust value-score deviation bound must be localized by policy disagreement mass and the polynomial propensity boundary before empirical welfare maximization.
s8-policy-regret.destination_search: The destination search found confounding-robust policy improvement and clean observational policy learning, but no Huber full-record weak-overlap regret theorem.
s8-policy-regret.cynical_objection: Immediate by inserting robust ATE scores into standard empirical welfare maximization.
s8-policy-regret.rebuttal: Uniform policy regret needs a localized robust empirical process and a matching policy lower bound; a scalar ATE error bound does not supply either.

s9-conformal.anchor_read: Read the robustate setup and inference sections, then searched conformal counterfactual and randomization-inversion papers for an exchangeability group compatible with the observed Huber mixture.
s9-conformal.question: Invert a permutation or conformal score to obtain finite-sample ATE uncertainty under corrupted weak-overlap records.
s9-conformal.first_changed_proof_step: The initial exchangeability or randomization-orbit step fails because observational treatment assignment is unknown and \(Q\) may replace all fields.
s9-conformal.destination_search: The search found conformal counterfactual inference with interventional calibration data and conformal inference for cluster randomized trials, neither of which supplies a valid orbit here.
s9-conformal.cynical_objection: No exact symmetry survives arbitrary full-record Huber contamination, so finite-sample permutation validity has no foundation.
s9-conformal.rebuttal: The objection holds on the declared data alone; adding validation or randomized data would change the experiment.
s9-conformal.anti_pattern_check: Rejected rather than forcing the cluster-default rate framing: the defining M17 symmetry is absent.

literature_map: The field-tier calibration is anchored against Section 3 and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 of MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 on clean weak-overlap trimming and bias correction, KhanTamer2010 on generic overlap-tail irregularity, ChenGaoRen2016 on Huber tests and neighborhood intersection, and SasakiUra2022Robustate on the applied consumer. None provides a finite dyadic estimator or a same-class lower pair under arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\) at a quadratic propensity boundary. The open multidimensional frontier is informed by RobinsEtAl2017HOEE and LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF on clean projected functional correction, BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024 on clean ATE nuisance-product frontiers, ZhuJiaoSteinhardt2022 on robust moment stability, and HaradaFujisawa2024 on robust causal scores. AgarwalSingh2022 instead imposes low-rank structured error and bounded propensity, while MaEtAl2024Missing treats finite-coordinate missingness. The 2024 conference program supplies only a talk title on contamination-resilient functional estimation and no publicly checkable theorem text, so it is disclosed without a comparator promise.

novelty_justification.published_axis: The nearest clean weak-overlap paper, MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026, constructs trimmed bias-corrected doubly robust estimators from clean i.i.d. observations in Section 3 and verifies the ATE boundary conditions in Appendix B, Proposition B.1, but it does not allow arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). ChenGaoRen2016 gives the abstract Huber modulus and collision devices without a fast scalar-functional estimator. The calibration theorem closes this exact gap on the full \(d=1,\alpha=\beta=1,\kappa=2\) class.
novelty_justification.repo_axis: The downgraded stat_ate_overlap_decay proposals omit full-record Huber contamination, and the accepted stat_discrete_ate_minimax_loggap proposal is clean with interior treatment probabilities. This core adds an explicit finite estimator, global point-or-diffuse contaminant accounting, and a same-class pair yielding both \(n^{-2/5}\) and \(\epsilon^{1/2}\) lower components; the general robust projection frontier remains open rather than being claimed solved.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic:
The statistical price of corrupted records under weak causal overlap. Fix d>=1, alpha,beta,kappa>0, L>=4. Clean observations O=(X,A,Y) lie in [0,1]^d x {0,1} x [0,1]. Under P, X is exactly uniform, e(x)=P(A=1|X=x)=x_1^kappa u(x), u in H^alpha(L) with 1/4<=u<=1/2, and mu_a(x)=E[Y|X=x,A=a] in H^beta(L) with 1/4<=mu_a<=3/4. Conditional outcome laws otherwise unrestricted. H^s(L) bounds all partial derivatives through m=ceil(s)-1 by L and order-m derivatives have (s-m)-Holder seminorm <=L under sup norm. At the boundary x_1=0, mu_1 is its unique continuous extension, not an independently identified conditional value. Clean consistency and conditional exchangeability identify theta(P)=integral_[0,1]^d (mu_1-mu_0) dx. Observe n>=2 iid records from R=(1-epsilon)P+epsilon Q, with known 0<=epsilon<=1/10 and Q any probability law on the same record space; Q may corrupt all three fields. Estimator knows d,alpha,beta,kappa,L,epsilon and clean covariate design, but not P,Q,u,mu_a. Fixed nonzero epsilon entails irreducible ambiguity; do not claim point identification of theta from R. For every fixed d,alpha,beta,kappa,L above and jointly for all n>=2 and 0<=epsilon<=1/10, determine an explicit deterministic evaluable rate rho(n,epsilon;d,alpha,beta,kappa,L), including logarithms at regime boundaries, such that c*rho <= inf_T sup_(P,Q) E_((1-epsilon)P+epsilon Q)^n |T-theta(P)| <= C*rho, over all Borel data-only estimators and exactly the declared clean-law/contamination class. Constants c,C may depend on the fixed class parameters but not n,epsilon. Supply a total finite computable attaining estimator with stated computation, and matching same-experiment converses. Derive the joint clean-functional, overlap and contamination transitions from primitives; resolve whether clean risk and the ATE total-variation modulus can be attained simultaneously or whether nuisance learning incurs an additional interaction penalty. Neither the max formula, an interaction, nor an exponent is assumed. A whole-law TV estimation bound, oracle known-nuisance rate, one-point contamination modulus or unmatched clipping bound alone does not discharge the kernel. Consumer: Sasaki and Ura (2022), Average treatment effect estimates robust to the limited overlap problem: robustate, Stata Journal, and its right-heart-catheterization analysis. The result separates robustness to limited overlap from robustness to corrupted records and provides an error-radius and trimming/boundary-correction benchmark when a fraction of records is unreliable. This is a theoretical benchmark on a known-design boundary class, not a claim that the published parametric-propensity workflow satisfies this class or that its actual data are corrupted. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1536867X221106402 PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derives the clean-ATE total-variation modulus delta^((beta+1)/(beta+kappa+1)), including changing propensity. On the full d=1, alpha=beta=1, kappa=2 class, unknown-nuisance cell means with variable widths and boundary extrapolation give the matched candidate rate n^(-2/5)+sqrt(epsilon). The draft supplies population bias, arbitrary full-record contamination, random-denominator and empty-cell arguments; exact witness and dyadic calculations were checked. These are unverified derivations, not the general theorem. A projected nuisance-product identity isolates the potential fast-functional gain, but naive pair correction incurs an explicit epsilon^2 times kernel-diagonal bias under concentrated contamination. Current comparisons did not identify a full-frontier collision; a 2024 robust-functional conference talk remains a literature lead to resolve.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct a finite robust projected correction with nuisance pilots and Gram matrix learned from corrupted records at resolutions above stable local occupancy, or prove a matching interaction penalty; complete the same-class converse and transition logarithms.
EARLY KILL TEST: Test the proposed correction on the exact finite-cell slab with a point contaminant and then diffuse contamination within one fine cell. Without a proved bound preserving the clean high-resolution gain or a matched interaction lower bound, abandon that estimator route. The solved Lipschitz regime must remain a consistency check.

message: Re-centered the core on the exact one-dimensional contaminated Lipschitz minimax theorem, repaired the point-contamination calculation, specified the dyadic estimator and same-experiment lower pair, retagged the controlled overlap assumptions, and anchored the clean-record comparator.

literature_checklist.author: Khan and Tamer
literature_checklist.one_line: Inverse-weight treatment-effect estimation can be irregular when identification requires arbitrarily large weights, with rates governed by tail support.

literature_checklist.author: Chen, Gao, and Ren
literature_checklist.one_line: Scheffé tests yield robust minimax procedures, and Huber lower bounds are controlled by a total-variation modulus.

literature_checklist.author: Robins et al.
literature_checklist.one_line: Projection-based higher-order estimating equations attain fast clean rates for missing-response means under low nuisance regularity.

literature_checklist.author: Liu et al.
literature_checklist.one_line: An empirical Gram construction yields clean semiparametric efficiency without estimating a smooth covariate density.

literature_checklist.author: Zhu, Jiao, and Steinhardt
literature_checklist.one_line: Generalized resilience turns robust moment stability into minimum-distance estimators under broad perturbations.

literature_checklist.author: Sasaki and Ura
literature_checklist.one_line: The robustate command implements bias-corrected trimmed IPW inference for limited overlap and illustrates it with right-heart-catheterization data.

literature_checklist.author: Harada and Fujisawa
literature_checklist.one_line: Density-power IPW and doubly robust scores resist outcome outliers, but naive robustification loses double robustness and requires correction.

literature_checklist.author: Bonvini et al.
literature_checklist.one_line: Second-order ATE corrections can improve clean nuisance-product rates in a hybrid smoothness and structure-agnostic model.

literature_checklist.author: Horowitz and Manski
literature_checklist.one_line: Contaminated sampling generally leaves the clean parameter unidentified, making identified bounds more natural than robust point recovery.

literature_checklist.author: Ma, Sant’Anna, Sasaki, and Ura
literature_checklist.one_line: Section 3 constructs trimmed bias-corrected doubly robust estimators from i.i.d. observations, and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies the ATE boundary conditions without arbitrary full-record replacement.
